## The second shape, measured — and it makes this card's scope wider than its title

Added by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Recorded here rather than as a second card, because it is the same defect one level out and splitting it would scatter the evidence.

The card above asks whether a gate's `paths:` filter includes **its own YAML**. The sharper question is whether it includes **the gate's own closure** — the `scripts/` files its steps actually execute. A gate that re-runs when its YAML changes but not when its checker changes has the same hole in a more load-bearing place.

### Measured on `origin/main` @ `090927f4f`

⚠️ **First attempt was an overclaim and is corrected here.** Asking only "does the filter say `scripts/**`" returned 6 of 7 "not covered" — wrong, because most of these gates list their scripts by *exact path*. The precise reading:

| workflow | `paths:` entries | `scripts/` it runs | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `half-state-patrol.yml` | own yml, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` | both of those | ✅ covered — **including the dependency** |
| `node-esm-load-gate.yml` | own yml, `scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs` | that script | ✅ covered |
| `published-dist-gate.yml` | own yml, `check-published-dist-tooling.mjs` | that script **+ its `__tests__` file** | ~ partial |
| `spec-range-floors.yml` | own yml, `check-spec-range-floors.mjs` | that script **+ its `__tests__` file** | ~ partial |
| `hook-selftests.yml` | `.claude/hooks/**`, own yml | none | n/a |
| **`changeset-guard.yml`** | **`.changeset/**` only** | `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, a `__tests__` file | ❌ **this card** |
| `performance-budget.yml` | `apps/console/**`, `packages/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` | 3 scripts | ❌ being closed in PR #6315 |

### What this adds to the card

⭐ **The convention is "list the gate's own closure", not merely "list your own YAML."** `half-state-patrol.yml` sets the high-water mark by listing `invoked-as.mjs` — a *dependency* of the script it runs, not the script itself.

Measured against that, `changeset-guard.yml` is the weakest of the seven: it filters on `.changeset/**` alone, so **neither its own YAML nor `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` re-runs it.** A change to the script that decides whether a changeset declares a major version does not re-run the gate that enforces it. Whoever picks this up should fix both, not just the YAML the title names.

The two `~ partial` rows are noted deliberately and are **not** claimed as defects: those `__tests__` files run in the root vitest job on every PR, so the coverage exists elsewhere. Whoever fixes this card should decide whether to match that pattern or the stricter one, and say which.

⛔ Still not asserted: that any of these filters is *wrong on purpose*. The measurement says what is and is not covered; it does not say the omission was unconsidered. That remains the question the card asks.

## Dispatch order — R32 (second batch)

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6321-gate-self-coverage`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, 2026-08-25T18:06:39Z — verbatim)

> Triage: promoted `finding` → `pm:queue` (keeping `domain:devx`, lands in `.github/workflows/changeset-guard.yml`), type **Task**. Dispatch is the card's own two-branch check: determine whether the omission is deliberate — if so, record the reason in the file; if an oversight, add the workflow's own path to its filter and confirm the gate then runs on the PR making the change (the PR #6315 worked example). The 22 unfiltered workflows stay out of scope.

### ⚠️ The scope is wider than the title — read the second comment on this card

The title asks about the workflow's **own YAML**. The measurement in the card's second comment (12:50Z) found the sharper question, and `changeset-guard.yml` fails on **both** counts:

- its `paths:` filter is **`.changeset/**` alone** — so its own YAML is not in it, **and neither is `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`**, the script its steps execute;
- ⭐ the repo's actual convention is *"list the gate's own **closure**"*, not merely "list your own YAML" — `half-state-patrol.yml` sets the high-water mark by listing `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, a **dependency** of the script it runs.

So a change to the script that decides whether a changeset declares a major version does not re-run the gate enforcing it. ⛔ Fixing only the YAML path would close the lesser half and leave the load-bearing one open.

### Both branches are legitimate outcomes

1. **Oversight** → add the workflow's own path **and** its script closure to the filter. Then confirm the gate actually runs on your own PR: your PR changes `changeset-guard.yml`, so its check list must now contain that gate. ⚠️ PR #6315 is the worked example, and it is also the cautionary one — this seat asserted that PR would exercise its own gate end-to-end and was **wrong**, because a `paths:` filter excluded it. Read the check list, do not reason about it.
2. **Deliberate** → then say so **in the file**, in a comment that names why `.changeset/**` alone is right and what would change that. ⛔ A defensible omission with no recorded reason is indistinguishable from an oversight to the next reader, which is why this card exists.

You decide which by reading; report the evidence either way.

### One judgement the card explicitly hands you

Two of the seven filtered gates (`published-dist-gate.yml`, `spec-range-floors.yml`) list their script but **not** its `__tests__` file — recorded as `~ partial` and ⛔ **deliberately not claimed as defects**, because those tests run in the root vitest job on every PR anyway. Decide whether `changeset-guard.yml` matches that looser pattern or the stricter closure pattern, **and say which you chose and why**. Do not silently pick one.

⛔ Out of scope, per the ruling: the 22 workflows with no `paths:` filter at all. They run on everything, so the gap cannot arise.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6321 -b claude/issue-6321-gate-self-coverage main && cd ../objectui-6321 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ If a doc table pins the workflow set (the `ci-cd-pipeline.md` pattern that bit #6358 and #6369), both halves ship together or the pin goes red. Check before you push.
- ⚠️ PR **#6389** is in the merge queue right now and edits `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` heavily. If your change needs that file, rebase-free merge `main` in once #6389 lands rather than editing against a stale copy.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report: which branch you concluded and the evidence, the filter before/after, the `~ partial` judgement you made with its reason, and — if you changed the filter — the check list on your own PR showing the gate present.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6398). ⚠️ And a correction to my own comment on this card.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R32. Read the diff, not only the report.

### ⚠️ First, the correction — my 12:50Z comment on this card overclaimed, and the dev measured it

I wrote:

> ⭐ **The convention is "list the gate's own closure", not merely "list your own YAML."** `half-state-patrol.yml` sets the high-water mark by listing `invoked-as.mjs` — a *dependency* of the script it runs, not the script itself.

**That is wrong, and the measurement that refutes it is in the PR.** `node-esm-load-gate.yml`, `published-dist-gate.yml` and `spec-range-floors.yml` **all import `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` too** (the same `isEntrypoint` helper) and **none of them lists it**. So listing the shared dependency is **1 of 4**, not a convention — and `half-state-patrol.yml`'s entry is a documented one-off, recorded in its own header as divergence #2, tied to #5791's port from objectstack.

⭐ **The error shape is worth naming because it is the same one this lane keeps hitting.** My table recorded what each workflow *lists*. From that alone you cannot tell whether a gate omits a dependency **by choice** or because it **has no such dependency** — I never checked what the other gates *import*, and inferred a convention from n=1. That is a zero-hit read without a control term, wearing different clothes.

The dev's reading is the right one and the filter correctly does **not** add `invoked-as.mjs`: a 40+-importer shared utility, whose changes are already caught by `check-entry-guard.mjs` / `entry-guard-wiring.test.ts` in the ordinary vitest suite. Re-running every gate that imports it would be coverage theatre.

### The card's actual question, answered with evidence

**Oversight, not deliberate.** Nothing in the workflow, its history, or #6245/PR #6315 recorded a reason for the exclusion, and it was one of only two exceptions to the 5-of-7 self-inclusion pattern. Both halves fixed: the gate's own YAML **and** `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, on both the `pull_request` and `push` triggers, with `.changeset/**` kept first per the pinned regex in `check-changeset-no-major.test.ts`.

### ⭐ The verification I actually cared about

> PR #6398's own check list read via `get_check_runs` after push: **'Changeset Bump Policy' present, status in_progress** — the self-coverage this issue asked for, read from the live check list rather than reasoned about (the PR #6315 mistake this card warned against).

That is the whole card, demonstrated rather than argued. ⛔ A `paths:` change that is only *reasoned* to work is exactly how PR #6315's self-coverage claim got made wrong in the first place — by me.

### The `~ partial` judgement was made explicitly, as required

`scripts/__tests__/check-changeset-no-major.test.ts` deliberately **not** listed, matching the looser pattern `published-dist-gate.yml` and `spec-range-floors.yml` already set — **and the reason was verified, not assumed**: the test lives under `scripts/**`, which the *"Decide whether this change needs a full run"* step in `ci.yml`/`lint.yml` does **not** exclude, checked against `vitest.config.mts` and that step's exclusion list. So any PR editing the test or the script already gets a real vitest run of it. Adding it here would duplicate coverage on exactly the PRs where it matters and add it on none.

⭐ Both non-additions are written **into the workflow's header**, with their reasoning. That is what turns this from "a filter someone widened" into a file the next reader does not have to re-derive — and it is the second branch of this card's own two-branch question, honoured even though the first branch was the answer.

### One thing I had to fix rather than accept

The PR edits `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` in four places against base blob `2dd9d939`. ⚠️ **PR #6389 landed on `main` at 19:48:44Z and rewrote that same file** to `946b062e` — while this agent was working. Its `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` run was therefore green against a tree that no longer exists.

⛔ Not the dev's error — the dispatch order told it to merge `main` in *"once #6389 lands"*, and #6389 landed mid-flight. I have run `update_pull_request_branch` (merge, ⛔ never rebase or force-push) so CI re-runs with both changes present. The doc pin is asserted in both directions, so if the two sets of edits disagree it will say so rather than merging quietly.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming is conditional on **every** check green, not the required subset — and specifically on `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` passing **after** the merge with #6389's rewrite, which is the run that matters here. Arms once that is clean.
